doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Europe and a single mother's career
title: Performing with George Russell at Newport and later
summary: She appeared with Russell's sextet at Newport in 1964, at the Modern Museum of Art and later in Boston, usually only to sing Sunshine.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well, okay. So, so, Sheila, after you recorded the Blue Note record. After you recorded the Outer View―You Are My Sunshine on the Outer View, uh, you appeared with George Russell Sextet at the Newport Jazz Festival in ‟64. You want to talk about that or any other performances you did with George?

Well, that, those were the only two I did. I mean, I did the Newport and then I did one at the museum, I think… Modern Museum of Art one time. I don‟t remember what that was for, but those are the only times that I, that I appeared with George, and it was only, it was only to do Sunshine. And then, uh, years later, up in Boston at, I think it was Jordan Hall, he was doing a concert and he had me come up, and I improvised on, I think, Stratosfunk, one of the blues lines. [singing] [laughs]
„cause that was [laughs], that was weird. Um… So were you still working at Page Three at that time? No?
